scope: read-only source review and bounded temporary-store tests; no V3 integration, production store, model or scientific job

tests.result: 14 tests passed in 0.346 seconds in independent rerun; the source's 12 barrier races again sampled seal-wins only, while held-transaction tests exercise both serialized orders.
tests.relevant_case: test_repeated_same_process_prepublication_errors_recover injects three os.link exceptions after each attempt temp file is written/fsynced; each attempt leaves an inert distinct name, and same-process finalize retry publishes identical DB-committed bytes and returns idempotently.

review.specific_v1_finding: V1's PID-only temp name could be stranded by an ordinary exception and block a same-process retry with FileExistsError.
review.v2_correction: V2 uses PID plus secrets.token_hex(16) in a fresh exclusive temp name per projection attempt. Repeated ordinary publication exceptions leave unique inert temps; they do not collide with or prevent retry. Exclusive final os.link, exact-byte conflict checking, directory fsync, and DB-authoritative final bytes remain intact.
review.empty_and_failure_semantics: Explicit-empty final disposition is distinct from nonempty success; failed/blocked/cancelled terminals produce terminal_with_failures; qualification remains unassessed. OPEN, pending and missing evidence block finalization. These are workflow bookkeeping labels, not scientific outcome validation.
review.crash_recovery: The existing process-exit tests cover pre/post enqueue, seal, terminal and final DB commits, plus before/after receipt publication and directory sync. Recovery from a committed final row projects the same canonical bytes. A stale temp after a process exit is harmless under the nonce scheme, though not scavenged.
review.store_versioning: The binding schema is FiniteIntakeCoreV2 and source/root checked; code rejects mismatched V1 binding rather than silently migrating. No migration path is established.

limitations: No actual queue-v3 adapter exists in this packet; the original V3 enqueue/seal race, partial-admission ownership/scaffolding crashes, executor reconciliation and reservation/liveness checks remain unresolved for integration.

Terminal evidence uses an invented fixture contract and a mutable local SQLite/filesystem trust model. No authentic V3 receipts, cryptographic producer identity, hostile same-user protection, scientific qualification or thousands-cycle capacity is established.

Tests assume an honest local Linux filesystem. They do not prove power-loss/device-flush behavior, NFS/network semantics, backup/restore, or eliminate all storage failures. Random temporary names solve accidental retry collision, not adversarial same-user attacks or garbage collection.
